attributes.body_ja:
「ということは」は主（おも）に文中（ぶんちゅう）に登場（とうじょう）し、前（まえ）に述（の）べられた内容（ないよう）を整理（せいり）するときに使（つか）われる表現（ひょうげん）です。「(A) であることは (B) を意味（いみ）する」というような意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。「ということは」を含（ふく）む文（ぶん）は、「ということだ」で終（お）わることが多（おお）いですが、必（かなら）ずそうなるわけではありません。

この表現（ひょうげん）は、話（はな）し手（て）が (A) を受（う）けて、それに対（たい）する説明（せつめい）が必要（ひつよう）であることを示（しめ）します。

また「ということは」は、話（はな）し手（て）が (A) について自分（じぶん）の理解（りかい）が正（ただ）しいかを確認（かくにん）したいときに、文（ぶん）の頭（あたま）で使（つか）われることもあります。この場合（ばあい）、疑問（ぎもん）文（ぶん）になることも多（おお）く、「つまり」などと言（い）い換（か）えることもできます。

「ということは」は「という」「こと」「は」に分解（ぶんかい）でき、「(A) という物事（ものごと）については（一般的（いっぱんてき）に） (B) だと理解（りかい）される」というニュアンスを持（も）っていると言（い）えます。
attributes.body:
ということは is a phrase in Japanese that often appears in the middle of sentences, expressing that the previous statement is something that is about to be clarified. This can be translated as 'that means', or 'that is to say'. ということは based sentences will often finish with ということだ, although it is not limited to appearing this way.

The more literal translation is something similar 'that which is said to be (A), (B)'. In this way, it simply presents (A) as a thing that requires further explaining.

Additionally, ということは will appear at the beginning of sentences, when the speaker is confirming their understanding about something that has just been said. Often in the form of a question. In these cases, the translation is similar 'so you mean to say that (A)?'.

As can be seen from the breakdown of という, こと, and は, this statement just expresses that the 'thing' which is 'classified as' (A) is 'in general' understood to be (B).

attributes.description: To summarize / boil down something, that means

attributes.body: ということ turns phrases into nouns and is often used to clarify what was said. When followed by は as ということは, it marks the phrase as a topic for further explanation or comment. ということは can also begin a sentence to restate or interpret what came before, like 'So what you're saying is (A)' in English.

second_relatable.title: ということは
second_relatable.meaning: That means, That is to say

attributes.body: というのは and ということは are similar in that both take a phrase and turn it into a topic for further explanation. While sometimes interchangeable, というのは is typically followed by a definition or reason. ということは is primarily used to rephrase, clarify, or draw a conclusion from the previous statement.

first_relatable.title: というのは
first_relatable.meaning: ~ Known as ~ is, ~ Called ~ is, ~ Means ~, Because

second_relatable.title: ということは
second_relatable.meaning: That means, That is to say

attributes.body: These two expressions are similar in that both can be used when offering or seeking explanations. ことなの is used at the end of a phrase or sentence, often to clarify a particular point, e.g. 今日は来ないということなの？ ('So does that mean he's not coming today?'), while ということは begins a sentence and sets up a conclusion based on what was just said, e.g. ということは、今日は来ないんだ ('So that means he's not coming today').

first_relatable.title: ことなの
first_relatable.meaning: (A) is (Description of A), (A) means that (Description of A)

second_relatable.title: ということは
second_relatable.meaning: That means, That is to say

attributes.body: つまり and ということは both rephrase earlier information, but differ in usage. つまり restates or explains something just said, e.g. つまりできないってこと？ ('So you're saying you can't do it?'). ということは introduces a logical inference or consequence, e.g. ということは、試合は中止だね ('So that means the game is canceled').

first_relatable.title: つまり
first_relatable.meaning: In short, To sum up, In other words

second_relatable.title: ということは
second_relatable.meaning: That means, That is to say

attributes.body: 即ち and ということは both rephrase information, but differ in tone and function. 即ち is formal and used to define or clarify precisely, often in writing, e.g. 日本の首都、即ち東京 ('The capital of Japan—namely, Tokyo'). ということは is conversational and introduces a conclusion, e.g. 明日は休み？ということは、今日は早く帰れるかもね ('Tomorrow's a holiday? So that means we might get to leave early today').
